sentence: Four-class Alzheimer MRI classification must separate adjacent stages whose scans can look structurally similar.
This experiment turns 6,400 folder-labelled MRI images into a complete TensorFlow workflow.
It inspects the scans, builds an 80-10-10 train, validation, and test pipeline, resizes images to 256 square pixels, and applies augmentation only to training data.
The primary convolutional network contains six convolution-and-pooling blocks, dropout, a dense representation, and a four-class softmax output.
Independently saved models are then compared through their full probability vectors, allowing uncertain judgments to be combined before the final class is chosen.
In the author-confirmed companion experiment, held-out accuracy increased from 78 to 85 percent.

What makes the project special is the visible experimental progression: data, tensors, architecture, individual predictions, model diversity, ensemble probabilities, and image-level error review all remain inspectable inside one reproducible notebook.
